ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which Arabic sentence means "I am from Kenya." (1 mark)
   A. اسْمِي أَحْمَدُ
   B. أَنَا تِلْمِيذَةٌ
   C. أَنَا مِنْ كينيا
   D. أَنَا تِلْمِيذٌ

2. What does the Arabic word كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ (kayfa haaluka?) mean? (1 mark)
   A. and upon you peace (the reply)
   B. welcome
   C. How are you? (to a boy)
   D. I

3. Which Arabic sentence means "I am a pupil (boy)." (1 mark)
   A. اسْمِي أَحْمَدُ
   B. أَنَا تِلْمِيذَةٌ
   C. أَنَا تِلْمِيذٌ
   D. أَنَا مِنْ كينيا

4. What does the Arabic sentence هَذِهِ أُمِّي mean? (1 mark)
   A. This is my father.
   B. I have a brother and a sister.
   C. My father works.
   D. This is my mother.

5. The cat is under the bed. Which position word is used? (1 mark)
   A. fii
   B. taHta
   C. fawqa
   D. ʿalaa

6. What does the Arabic word مَدْرَسَةٌ (madrasa) mean? (1 mark)
   A. Monday
   B. day
   C. yesterday
   D. school

7. What does the Arabic word اِسْمَعْ (ismaʿ) mean? (1 mark)
   A. open the door
   B. read
   C. write
   D. listen

8. Which Arabic sentence means "Do you have a party? (to a boy)" (1 mark)
   A. عِيدُ مِيلَادٍ سَعِيدٌ
   B. عِيدٌ مُبَارَكٌ
   C. كُلَّ عَامٍ وَأَنْتُمْ بِخَيْرٍ
   D. هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَفْلَةٌ؟

9. What does the Arabic word حَلْوَى (halwaa) mean? (1 mark)
   A. festival
   B. sweets
   C. my turn
   D. no

10. What does the Arabic word يَدٌ (yad) mean? (1 mark)
   A. tooth
   B. hand
   C. mouth
   D. stomach

11. What does the Arabic word فَمٌ (fam) mean? (1 mark)
   A. mouth
   B. tongue
   C. face
   D. hair

12. What does the Arabic sentence الْجَوُّ حَارٌّ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The weather is hot.
   B. The weather is rainy.
   C. The weather is cloudy.
   D. The weather is cold.

13. How do you read the syllable مَ? (1 mark)
   A. bi
   B. ma
   C. lu
   D. si

14. How do you read the syllable لِ? (1 mark)
   A. ti
   B. qaa
   C. muu
   D. li

15. How do you read the syllable ثَا? (1 mark)
   A. thaa
   B. sa
   C. qaa
   D. lu

16. The sentence ʿalaa t-taawilati kuub says where a cup is. Where is it? (1 mark)
   A. In the bag
   B. Under the bed
   C. On the table
   D. At the door

17. In what order do you say the letters when you spell an Arabic word aloud? (1 mark)
   A. In any order
   B. From left to right
   C. From the last letter only
   D. From right to left

18. Which sentence means 'On the table there is a cake'? (1 mark)
   A. hadiyya li-Aminata
   B. ʿalaa t-taawilati kaʿka
   C. haadhihi hafla
   D. fawqa t-taawilati baaluun

19. Which Arabic word means "big"? (1 mark)
   A. كَبِيرٌ
   B. دَجَاجٌ
   C. تَفَضَّلْ
   D. الْخَمِيسُ

20. How is the Arabic word دَجَاجٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. aruzz
   B. bayd
   C. sukkar
   D. dajaaj

21. Which Arabic sentence means "My body is strong." (1 mark)
   A. هَذَا جِسْمِي
   B. لِي يَدَانِ
   C. جِسْمِي قَوِيٌّ
   D. لِي عَيْنَانِ

22. How is the Arabic word جَوٌّ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ghaa'im
   B. jamiil
   C. jaww
   D. zahra

23. What does the Arabic sentence لَا تَلْعَبْ بِالسِّكِّينِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The key is in the cupboard.
   B. The chair is at the door.
   C. Do not play with the knife.
   D. I eat bread.

24. Which Arabic word means "in"? (1 mark)
   A. بِجَانِبِ
   B. فِي
   C. خَلْفَ
   D. عِنْدَ

25. What is the name of the Arabic letter ط? (1 mark)
   A. Haa
   B. waaw
   C. Taa
   D. alif

26. Which letter has one dot above it? (1 mark)
   A. ب (baa)
   B. ن (nuun)
   C. ي (yaa)
   D. ت (taa)

27. Which Arabic word means "clock"? (1 mark)
   A. مِصْبَاحٌ
   B. سَاعَةٌ
   C. غُرْفَةٌ
   D. كُرْسِيٌّ

28. Which Arabic word means "friend"? (1 mark)
   A. مَبْرُوكٌ
   B. أُغْنِيَةٌ
   C. تَفَضَّلْ
   D. صَدِيقٌ

29. What should you write on the back of a body flashcard? (1 mark)
   A. The sound and the meaning
   B. A long story
   C. Nothing
   D. Only your name

30. How does rain help people? (1 mark)
   A. It makes crops die
   B. It has no use
   C. It stops all farming
   D. It helps crops to grow and gives us water

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. A four-line poem says: ʿaynii taraa, udhunii tasmaʿu, anfii yashummu, famii yatakallamu. Give the meaning of the first line and say what the poem is about. (3 marks) (3 marks)

32. Put these syllables in order to make a family word and give its meaning: khaa + lun. (2 marks) (2 marks)

33. Write three instructions about the body in Arabic sounds with meanings. (3 marks) (3 marks)

34. Translate into English: al-asdiqaa'u fii l-hafla (2 marks)

35. Give two ways of taking care of your body. (2 marks) (2 marks)

36. Explain how a family celebration you know helps people to live together in peace. (3 marks) (3 marks)

37. Give two polite words for interrupting or inviting someone to speak, with meanings. (2 marks) (2 marks)

38. Write in Arabic sounds and translate: 'The weather is cold.' (2 marks) (2 marks)

39. Arrange these sentences into a good paragraph and give a reason: uhibbu baytii / haadhaa baytii / baytii kabiir. (3 marks) (3 marks)

40. Give three tips that help a speaker to use tone and pace well. (3 marks) (3 marks)

41. Translate into English: al-asdiqaa'u ya'kuluuna l-kaʿka (2 marks)

42. Translate into English: haadhihi ghurfatii (2 marks)

43. Translate into English: aqraʾu kitaaban yawma l-ahad (2 marks)

44. Put these words in order and translate: الْحَفْلَةَ / أُحِبُّ / أَنَا. (3 marks) (3 marks)

45. Name three verbal cues and say how each one helps the listener. (3 marks) (3 marks)

46. Translate into English: hadiyya li-Aminata (2 marks)

47. Name three things that make Arabic writing different from English writing. (3 marks) (3 marks)

48. Explain why a speaker should practise before speaking to an audience. (2 marks) (2 marks)

49. Write in Arabic sounds a question and an answer about bananas and give the meaning. (4 marks) (4 marks)

50. Look at a picture of a birthday party with a cake with a candle and friends standing round the table. Make a prediction and give a reason. (2 marks) (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — أَنَا مِنْ كينيا
   أَنَا مِنْ كينيا (anaa min Kiiniya) means: I am from Kenya.

2. C — How are you? (to a boy)
   كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ (kayfa haaluka?) means How are you? (to a boy).

3. C — أَنَا تِلْمِيذٌ
   أَنَا تِلْمِيذٌ (anaa tilmiidh) means: I am a pupil (boy).

4. D — This is my mother.
   هَذِهِ أُمِّي (haadhihi ummii) means: This is my mother.

5. B — taHta
   taHta means under.

6. D — school
   مَدْرَسَةٌ (madrasa) means school.

7. D — listen
   اِسْمَعْ (ismaʿ) means listen.

8. D — هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَفْلَةٌ؟
   هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَفْلَةٌ؟ (hal ʿindaka hafla?) means: Do you have a party? (to a boy)

9. B — sweets
   حَلْوَى (halwaa) means sweets.

10. B — hand
   يَدٌ (yad) means hand.

11. A — mouth
   فَمٌ (fam) means mouth.

12. A — The weather is hot.
   الْجَوُّ حَارٌّ (al-jawwu haarr) means: The weather is hot.

13. B — ma
   مَ is read ma.

14. D — li
   لِ is read li.

15. A — thaa
   ثَا is read thaa.

16. C — On the table
   ʿalaa t-taawilati kuub means 'on the table there is a cup'.

17. D — From right to left
   We spell Arabic in the direction it is written, from right to left.

18. B — ʿalaa t-taawilati kaʿka
   ʿalaa means on, taawila is table and kaʿka is cake.

19. A — كَبِيرٌ
   كَبِيرٌ (kabiir) means big.

20. D — dajaaj
   دَجَاجٌ is read dajaaj and means chicken.

21. C — جِسْمِي قَوِيٌّ
   جِسْمِي قَوِيٌّ (jismii qawiyy) means: My body is strong.

22. C — jaww
   جَوٌّ is read jaww and means weather.

23. C — Do not play with the knife.
   لَا تَلْعَبْ بِالسِّكِّينِ (laa talʿab bi-s-sikkiin) means: Do not play with the knife.

24. B — فِي
   فِي (fii) means in.

25. C — Taa
   The letter ط is called Taa.

26. B — ن (nuun)
   nuun has one dot above. Baa has one dot below, taa has two dots above and yaa has two dots below.

27. B — سَاعَةٌ
   سَاعَةٌ (saaʿa) means clock.

28. D — صَدِيقٌ
   صَدِيقٌ (sadiiq) means friend.

29. A — The sound and the meaning
   The Arabic word is on the front. The back has the sound and the meaning.

30. D — It helps crops to grow and gives us water
   Rain waters crops and fills rivers and tanks.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: My eye sees. The poem says what a part of the body does: the eye sees, the ear hears, the nose smells and the mouth speaks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning of the line and 2 marks for the poem's idea.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: khaa-lun (mother's brother).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the correct order and 1 mark for the meaning.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: irfaʿ yadaka (raise your hand), ilmis anfaka (touch your nose), aghmiD ʿaynayka (close your eyes).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct instruction with meaning.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: The friends are at the party.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands and face; clean teeth; eat good food; sleep well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible way.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: People meet, share food and joy, sing and talk together, and learn to respect one another.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meeting, 1 mark for sharing, 1 mark for respect.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: ʿafwan (excuse me) and tafaddal (please, go ahead).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each word with meaning.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: al-jawwu baarid. The weather is cold.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the Arabic sounds and 1 mark for the translation.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: haadhaa baytii. baytii kabiir. uhibbu baytii. The topic comes first, then a detail, then the feeling at the end.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the first sentence, 1 mark for the order and 1 mark for the reason.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Speak loudly enough and clearly; speak at a steady speed; pause between sentences; smile when greeting.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid tip.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: The friends eat the cake.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is my room.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: I read a book on Sunday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: أَنَا أُحِبُّ الْحَفْلَةَ. I like the party.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the first word, 1 mark for the correct order and 1 mark for the translation.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Intonation shows questions and statements; speed shows importance or excitement; tonal variation shows feeling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each cue with its use.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: A gift for Amina.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is written from right to left; it has no capital letters; most letters join and change shape; short vowels are shown with marks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid difference.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Practice helps the speaker to remember words, pronounce them correctly and feel less nervous.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for remembering or pronouncing and 1 mark for confidence.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: hal tuhibbu l-mawz? naʿam, uhibbu l-mawz. Do you like bananas? Yes, I like bananas.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence and 1 mark for each meaning.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: The friends will sing and eat the cake, because the cake has a candle and they stand round the table.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a sensible prediction and 1 mark for a reason from the picture.
